Matchup-Driven

There's no bell-cow to bank on — the lead back sees just 50% of carries (league ~59%), a committee that caps any one back's ceiling and makes their rushing props matchup- and script-dependent.

The Offensive Blueprint

In the passing game the ball funnels to their WR1 — 29% of targets (league ~23%), a genuine alpha share that concentrates the receiving value at the top.

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 18% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

They're a heavy under-center team (61% shotgun vs ~68%) — a pro-style, run-committed structure.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 59% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is run-first (47% pass), funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — No Obvious Seam

They lock down opposing WR1s — just 48 rec yds/game (vs ~58); fade receiving props there.

Soft against opposing tight ends — 42 rec yds/game (vs ~35). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 106 rushing and 226 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

A stingy, efficient defense — just 42% success allowed (vs ~44%); temper expectations for opposing skill players.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs).

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
